How this applet works

A searchable index you can inspect

Click Build embeddings, wait for the index, then describe a topic. Every book stays in the results. Select one to see field scores and matching text.

Available information

The LibraryThing Summary column contains generated citations in this test catalog. Citations are preserved but excluded from synopsis embeddings. Subjects and Dewey wording are separate search fields. They are not converted into themes or genres.

Scoring

E5 small v2 produces 384-dimensional vectors using mean pooling, unit normalization, and its query: / passage: prefixes. Each field score is a dot product.

Whole-book focus: compare the query with each field's normalized mean of chunk vectors. Specific coverage: use each field's strongest chunk. Both combine available field scores by a weighted mean. The composite is not a probability. A field weighted zero does not affect the composite. Missing information does not prove irrelevance. More chunks give more chances for a strong match in coverage mode.

Text is chunked and checked against a 480-token limit to prevent silent truncation. E5 small is designed for English. Compare rankings and evidence rather than interpreting absolute scores as confidence.

Relative similarity and regression

Relative similarity is the default. For each query, the lowest scored book in the full catalog maps to 0 and the highest to 1. Each field column is scaled independently. Composite is calculated from raw field similarities before scaling. Missing scores stay empty. Identical scores map to 0.5. Filters do not change these reference ranges. Relative values indicate position within this catalog, not an absolute relevance probability.

Book-score Pearson r and the reported regression slope always use paired relative composite scores for the books currently shown. The regression fits Y = slope × X + intercept. Positive min–max scaling preserves Pearson r when both axes have variance, while changing the slope. The dashed line fits the displayed scale; raw mode therefore draws a raw-score fit. Undefined fits/correlations are labeled explicitly.

PDFs, repositories, and chapters

Use Add PDF / metadata or the selected book's Add source button. PDF.js reads local text, bookmarks, and metadata; optional Tesseract OCR handles English scans. Runtime and OCR model files download on first use. Detected abstract/summary, contents, glossary, index, keywords, and full text can fill fields after review. Themes and genre are not guessed. PDF bookmarks are preferred for sections; detected headings are a fallback. With no structure, clearly labeled page groups are used. Check boundaries and extracted fields before applying.

Internet Archive and Google Books lookups require an exact ISBN match. Existing text is kept unless you select a replacement. Google categories are treated as subjects. Public Archive OCR text is optional; restricted files are skipped. Google Books needs an API key, entered only for the current dialog session and excluded from backups. Provider errors are shown without discarding successful results.

Build embeddings after adding material. Full text is a separate weighted search field. Where possible, its vectors reuse chapter embeddings. Chapters and sections are ranked for each active query; contents-only records are explicitly marked as title-only matches. Relative chapter scores use the chapter list within that book as their reference.

Comparing queries and sorting

Two-query plot: enter separate X and Y queries. Each book is plotted at its weighted composite score for each query, using the same field weights and ranking method. Axes stay at 0–1; in raw mode, negative raw scores appear at zero. Missing scores are excluded from the plot.

Embedding cosine is the normalized dot product between the two query vectors. Embedding Pearson r correlates their vector components. Book-score Pearson r correlates paired relative composite scores across the books currently shown, including title/author and assignment filters. These three measures range from −1 to 1. Pearson r is undefined with fewer than two pairs or no variance. The embedding cosine is the semantic similarity measure; component correlation also depends on the embedding coordinate system. A high score correlation means the queries rank books similarly, not that the queries mean the same thing.

Click a ranking column once for highest to lowest, then again for lowest to highest. Missing values stay last. Hover or focus a Composite score or heading to edit the shared field weights; on touch screens use the ▾ button. A value of zero excludes that field.

Saving and updating

This browser saves data and embeddings in IndexedDB when available. Export data downloads a portable JSON backup with text, vectors, categories, and assignments. Save applet downloads an HTML copy with the current data embedded. The model weights are not embedded.

Import a LibraryThing TSV/CSV/Excel catalog or an applet JSON backup. Catalog imports merge by Book Id, keep unchanged embeddings, and preserve manual edits. They do not delete records absent from a filtered export. JSON backups restore the whole saved state.

Use Add ISBNs to paste ISBN-10/ISBN-13 identifiers or load a plain list. Open Library lookups fill empty fields when metadata is available and retain a source URL for each field. Equivalent ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 values are deduplicated. Existing text and manual edits are preserved. Missing matches are kept as unresolved ISBN entries with empty text vectors. Glossaries and full indexes are not fetched. This version does not poll LibraryThing.

Local computation

The runtime and model download from jsDelivr and Hugging Face on first use. Excel imports load SheetJS from its official CDN. Book text and queries are processed inside your browser with no hosted inference API. ISBN lookup sends only the identifiers you select to Open Library. Responses are cached, batched, and limited to no more than one request per second. Browser storage and model caching are subject to your browser's policies.

Downloaded HTML files now calculate embeddings directly in the browser tab. Hosted copies use a background worker with automatic fallback. If your browser blocks model downloads, you can also serve its folder with python -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 and open http://127.0.0.1:8765/library_semantic_search.html.
